key_question: How does water shape the land around us?
subject: Geography
model_text: Rivers are powerful forces that shape the land around us.

lessons.key_question: How does water shape the land around us?

learning_label.lf: I am learning to describe the key features of a river.
learning_label.sc1: I can name the three stages of a river.
learning_label.sc2: I can explain how rivers shape the land over time.

lessons.what: Identify and name key river features
lessons.why: Understanding river features helps us explain how water shapes the landscape
lessons.success: I can label a river diagram and describe what happens at each stage

vocabulary.definition: A large natural stream of water flowing towards the sea, a lake or another river
The starting point of a river, usually high up in hills or mountains
A smaller river or stream that joins a larger river
A curve or bend in a river, formed as water erodes the outer bank

lessons.lesson_flow: Introduce key river vocabulary. Label a river diagram together. Pupils sort river feature cards.

slides.title: What makes a river?
slides.content: A river has three main stages: the upper course (fast, steep), the middle course (wider, slower) and the lower course (wide, flat, near the sea).

slides.title: Label the river
slides.content: Together we label the main features on a river diagram — source, tributary, meander, flood plain, mouth.

slides.title: Sort the features
slides.content: In your trio, sort the river feature cards into upper, middle and lower course.

slides.title: River diagram
slides.content: Label and annotate your own river diagram LP.

questions: What is the source of a river?
What is a meander and how does it form?
Which stage of a river is fastest — upper, middle or lower?

lessons.key_question: How does water shape the land around us?

learning_label.lf: I am learning to explain how rivers erode and deposit material.
learning_label.sc1: I can describe what erosion means and give an example.
learning_label.sc2: I can explain the difference between erosion and deposition.

lessons.why: Erosion and deposition are the main processes that change the shape of rivers over time
lessons.success: I can explain what erosion and deposition mean and where they happen in a river

vocabulary.definition: The wearing away of rock and soil by water, wind or ice
When a river drops the material it has been carrying because it slows down
Tiny particles of rock, sand or soil carried and deposited by a river
The flat land beside a river that floods when the river overflows its banks
The wide mouth of a river where it meets the sea and fresh water mixes with salt water

quiz.question: What is the source of a river?
quiz.answer: The starting point of a river, usually high up in hills or mountains

quiz.question: Name the three stages of a river.
quiz.answer: Upper course, middle course and lower course

quiz.question: What is a meander?
quiz.answer: A curve or bend in a river formed as water erodes the outer bank

quiz.question: What is a tributary?
quiz.answer: A smaller river or stream that joins a larger river

lessons.lesson_flow: Recap river features. Explore erosion and deposition with sand tray. Record observations.

slides.title: Erosion and deposition
slides.content: Erosion happens fastest on the outer bend of a meander. Deposition happens on the inner bend where the water slows down. Over time this makes the meander more pronounced.

slides.title: Sand tray investigation
slides.content: Watch water flowing over the sand tray. Where does erosion happen? Where does deposition happen? Record observations as a class.

slides.title: Predict and explain
slides.content: In your trio, predict what will happen if we pour more water into the channel. Then explain what you saw using the words erosion and deposition.

slides.title: Erosion diagram
slides.content: Annotate a meander diagram to show where erosion and deposition happen. Explain why using a sentence.

questions: What is the difference between erosion and deposition?
Where in a meander does erosion happen fastest?
